title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 2nd Truth Divine Speech

questions.question: What is the main topic of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains that Allah’s speech is one of the great proofs of His existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute is being discussed at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What picture does the verse give by talking about the sea becoming ink?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s words are so many that even a huge ocean would not be enough to write them all.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how great Allah’s speech is?
questions.answer: It says it has no limit.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is one of the clearest signs that a being exists?
questions.answer: Speaking is one of the clearest signs.

questions.question: If speech shows that a being exists, what does Allah’s speech show?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah truly exists.

questions.question: Besides showing existence, what else does Divine speech prove?
questions.answer: It also proves Allah is One.

questions.question: Which two strong proofs of this truth are named first?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What other kind of proof is mentioned after revelation and inspiration?
questions.answer: Holy books sent from heaven.

questions.question: Which book is described as the brightest and widest proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage send readers to other sections for more details?
questions.answer: Because those sections explain and prove this truth more fully.

questions.question: What does the passage say is enough for the traveler at this point?
questions.answer: The meanings and spiritual lights found in the verse are enough for him.

questions.question: Why did the traveler stop and not go farther?
questions.answer: He was not able to continue beyond that point.

questions.question: What does the verse from Surah Al-Imran say Allah, the angels, and people of knowledge do?
questions.answer: They bear witness that only Allah deserves to be worshipped.

questions.question: What quality of Allah is connected with fairness in that verse?
questions.answer: He stands firmly with justice.

questions.question: In the lesson of the sacred station, what belief is stated again and again?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does “Necessary Existent” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means Allah truly exists and does not depend on anything else.

questions.question: What does the passage say belongs to Allah in a most beautiful way?
questions.answer: The most beautiful names, the highest attributes, and the loftiest example belong to Him.

questions.question: What agrees together in pointing to Allah’s necessary existence in unity?
questions.answer: His sacred attributes, His beautiful names, and His ruling actions all agree together.

questions.question: Name two kinds of actions mentioned that show Allah’s rule over creation.
questions.answer: Bringing things into existence and regulating them.

questions.question: What do will and power have to do with Allah’s actions in the passage?
questions.answer: They are connected with His creating and bringing things into being.

questions.question: What do choice and wisdom have to do with Allah’s actions in the passage?
questions.answer: They are connected with measuring, shaping, and managing creation.

questions.question: What do purpose and mercy have to do with Allah’s actions in the passage?
questions.answer: They are connected with providing, protecting, ordering, and caring for creation.

questions.question: What do complete order and balance in creation point to?
questions.answer: They point to Allah’s greatness and unity.

questions.question: What did the truths in the Nineteen Degrees mainly prove in the first chapter?
questions.answer: They mainly proved Allah’s necessary existence.

questions.question: Did those same truths also point to Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: Yes, they also showed His unity and oneness.

questions.question: In the second chapter, how will those truths be treated differently?
questions.answer: They will be presented mainly as proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: How are necessity and unity related in the passage?
questions.answer: Each one supports and proves the other.

questions.question: What wording was used often in the first chapter to show the truth’s greatness?
questions.answer: A phrase about the testimony of the greatness and broadness of the truth was used again and again.

questions.question: What different wording will be used in the second chapter?
questions.answer: A phrase about the witnessing or clearly seen greatness of the truth will be used.

questions.question: Why does the writer say the second chapter will be short?
questions.answer: Because different difficulties kept him from explaining it fully.

questions.question: Where does the writer leave the fuller explanation of these matters?
questions.answer: He leaves it to other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What truth is introduced at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: The truth of Divine speech.

questions.question: From which attribute does Divine speech come?
questions.answer: It comes from the attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the verse about the sea and ink?
questions.answer: Allah’s words are endless and cannot be fully counted.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the size or amount of Divine speech?
questions.answer: It describes it as without end.

questions.question: What human action is used as a sign that someone exists?
questions.answer: Speaking.

questions.question: Why is Divine speech called an endless testimony?
questions.answer: Because it keeps pointing to Allah’s existence and His unity.

questions.question: What are the first two strong proofs named for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What group of writings gives another wide proof?
questions.answer: The sacred books from heaven.

questions.question: Which revealed book is singled out for special praise?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What is special about the Qur’an in this passage?
questions.answer: It is described as a very shining and complete proof.

questions.question: Why are readers directed to other degrees of the work?
questions.answer: Those sections explain this truth in a fuller way.

questions.question: What is enough for both the readers and the traveler at this stage?
questions.answer: The guidance and deep meanings found in the verse.

questions.question: What does the verse from Surah Al-Imran teach about worship?
questions.answer: Only Allah deserves worship.

questions.question: Who joins Allah in giving witness in that verse?
questions.answer: The angels and people who have knowledge.

questions.question: What character trait of Allah is stressed in that verse along with His might and wisdom?
questions.answer: His justice.

questions.question: What short statement sums up the traveler’s lesson at this station?
questions.answer: Allah alone is God.

questions.question: In that summary statement, how is Allah described in relation to names and attributes?
questions.answer: He is the One who has the most beautiful names and the highest attributes.

questions.question: What points to Allah’s necessary existence in His unity?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent essence does, along with all His attributes and names.

questions.question: Do Allah’s names appear in disagreement or in harmony in this passage?
questions.answer: They appear in harmony and agreement.

questions.question: What do Allah’s actions do along with His names and attributes?
questions.answer: They also witness to His existence and oneness.

questions.question: Name one action in the passage that shows Allah creates.
questions.answer: Bringing things into existence.

questions.question: Name one action in the passage that shows Allah organizes creation.
questions.answer: Regulating creation.

questions.question: Name one action in the passage that shows Allah cares for creation.
questions.answer: Nurturing or preserving it.

questions.question: What two qualities are linked with Allah’s caring actions?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What do order and balance in the world help prove?
questions.answer: They help prove Allah’s greatness and His unity.

questions.question: In the first chapter, why were the truths treated mainly as proofs of necessary existence?
questions.answer: Because they showed existence in the clearest and most direct way.

questions.question: In the second chapter, what will these truths show more openly?
questions.answer: They will show Divine unity more openly.

questions.question: What do these truths still show in a less direct way in the second chapter?
questions.answer: They still show necessary existence.

questions.question: How does the passage connect unity and necessary existence?
questions.answer: It says each one proves the other.

questions.question: What was the writer planning to do for the second chapter?
questions.answer: He planned to explain its degrees in detail.

questions.question: Why was that plan not completed here?
questions.answer: Because of different obstacles.

questions.question: What does the writer choose to do instead?
questions.answer: He gives a brief and concise treatment.

questions.question: What Divine attribute is the focus of “The Second Truth”?
questions.answer: Allah’s Speech.

questions.question: What comes from this attribute according to the passage?
questions.answer: Divine discourse or Divine speaking comes from it.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention an ocean turning into ink?
questions.answer: To help us understand that Allah’s words are beyond counting.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the limit of Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: It has no limit.

questions.question: What everyday sign is used to show that someone is really there?
questions.answer: The sign of speech.

questions.question: When this idea is applied to Allah, what does it become?
questions.answer: It becomes a strong proof that Allah exists.

questions.question: What second belief does this proof support besides existence?
questions.answer: It supports Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Which two ways of receiving Divine messages are named as major proofs?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What is another proof besides those two?
questions.answer: The holy books from heaven.

questions.question: Which book is given the highest place among those proofs in this passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage avoid giving a long explanation here?
questions.answer: Because detailed explanations are already found in other parts.

questions.question: What are readers told is enough for now?
questions.answer: The guidance, light, and deep meaning in the verse.

questions.question: What did the traveler learn at this sacred station?
questions.answer: He learned that only Allah is truly God.

questions.question: Which other beings are named as witnesses along with Allah?
questions.answer: Angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: What does their witness agree on?
questions.answer: That there is no god except Allah.

questions.question: Which two qualities of Allah are named at the end of that verse?
questions.answer: Mighty and Wise.

questions.question: In the summary statement, how is Allah described in number?
questions.answer: He is described as One and Unique.

questions.question: What belongs to Allah according to that summary statement?
questions.answer: The beautiful names, the highest attributes, and the loftiest likeness belong to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s essence and His attributes?
questions.answer: His essence is necessarily existent and all His sacred attributes agree in pointing to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s names?
questions.answer: All His beautiful names, as they appear, agree in showing His necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: His active and ruling deeds also agree in giving the same witness.

questions.question: Which pair of qualities is connected with creating and originating?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: Which pair is connected with measuring, shaping, and directing?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: Which pair is connected with arranging, guarding, managing, and feeding?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: How do order and equilibrium strengthen the message of the passage?
questions.answer: They show that Allah’s actions are not random but full of perfection and unity.

questions.question: What did each of the nineteen truths do in the first chapter besides proving existence?
questions.answer: Each one also testified to Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: Why were they still counted first as proofs of necessary existence?
questions.answer: Because that was the clearest thing they showed.

questions.question: How will the same truths be named in the second chapter?
questions.answer: They will be named as proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the connection between the two truths of unity and necessity?
questions.answer: One leads to and confirms the other.

questions.question: What change in wording will mark the second chapter?
questions.answer: It will use a phrase that points more to clearly seeing unity.

questions.question: Did the writer want to explain the second chapter as fully as the first one?
questions.answer: Yes, that was his intention.

questions.question: Why is the explanation shorter than intended?
questions.answer: Because various obstacles forced him to be brief.

questions.question: What is the heading of the truth explained in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of Divine discourse.

questions.question: Which attribute is the source of Divine discourse?
questions.answer: The attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What does the image of a sea of ink help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader understand that Allah’s words are endless.

questions.question: According to the passage, can Divine speech be fully measured or counted?
questions.answer: No, it is infinite.

questions.question: What does the passage call one of the most obvious signs that someone exists?
questions.answer: That person’s speech.

questions.question: Why is this important in talking about Allah?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s speech becomes a proof of His existence.

questions.question: What two big beliefs are supported by Divine speech?
questions.answer: Allah’s existence and His unity.

questions.question: Which two proofs are said to be strong evidences of this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What gives another wide proof after those two?
questions.answer: The sacred books from heaven.

questions.question: What gives the most shining and complete proof?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why does the passage point readers elsewhere for full explanation?
questions.answer: Because those truths have already been discussed in other degrees.

questions.question: What is enough for the traveler who stopped at this point?
questions.answer: The spiritual lights and meanings inside the verse.

questions.question: In the quoted verse from Surah Al-Imran, what does Allah testify to?
questions.answer: That no one has the right to be worshipped except Him.

questions.question: Who else testifies to this in the verse?
questions.answer: The angels and people of knowledge.

questions.question: What does the verse say about Allah’s way of dealing with justice?
questions.answer: He stands firmly in justice.

questions.question: Which two names of Allah are mentioned at the end of that verse?
questions.answer: The Mighty and the Wise.

questions.question: In the statement that follows, how is Allah described in uniqueness?
questions.answer: He is described as One and absolutely unique.

questions.question: What special things are said to belong to Allah alone?
questions.answer: His beautiful names, supreme attributes, and the highest likeness.

questions.question: What part of Allah is said to point to His necessary existence in unity?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent essence.

questions.question: What joins with His essence in giving this proof?
questions.answer: All His sacred attributes, beautiful names, and ruling deeds.

questions.question: What kinds of actions show Allah’s continuing activity in the world?
questions.answer: Creating, making, bringing forth, shaping, regulating, preserving, administering, and giving sustenance.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with creating actions?
questions.answer: Will and power.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with regulating actions?
questions.answer: Choice and wisdom.

questions.question: Which qualities are linked with preserving and nurturing actions?
questions.answer: Purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the order and balance found in these actions?
questions.answer: They are complete and they witness to Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: In the first chapter, what were the nineteen truths mainly used to prove?
questions.answer: Allah’s necessary existence.

questions.question: Did they also support another belief?
questions.answer: Yes, they also supported Allah’s unity and oneness.

questions.question: What will be the main use of those truths in the second chapter?
questions.answer: They will mainly be used as proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: What hidden or less direct truth will they still show there?
questions.answer: They will still imply necessary existence.

questions.question: What important relationship between unity and necessity does the passage teach?
questions.answer: Unity proves necessity, and necessity proves unity.

questions.question: Why does the writer say he must be brief?
questions.answer: Because several obstacles kept him from giving a full explanation.

questions.question: Where should a reader look for a fuller explanation?
questions.answer: In other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What truth begins with the words “The Second Truth”?
questions.answer: The truth about Allah’s Divine speech.

questions.question: What attribute does this truth come from?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah’s attribute of Speech.

questions.question: How does the verse about the sea and ink help explain Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah’s words are far more than creation could ever write down.

questions.question: What word best describes the amount of Divine discourse in the passage?
questions.answer: Infinite.

questions.question: What is said to be a very clear sign of existence?
questions.answer: Speech.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from Allah’s speech?
questions.answer: That Allah exists and is One.

questions.question: Why is this testimony called infinite?
questions.answer: Because the proof coming from Divine speech has no end.

questions.question: Which two proofs are mentioned first for this truth?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What is named as another large proof after those?
questions.answer: The heavenly books.

questions.question: Which heavenly book is praised most in this passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about the Qur’an as a proof?
questions.answer: It is a very bright and wide-reaching proof of Allah’s speech.

questions.question: Why does the author not explain all of this in full here?
questions.answer: Because other sections already give those explanations and proofs.

questions.question: What is enough for the traveler at this point in the journey?
questions.answer: The light and wisdom contained in the verse.

questions.question: What lesson from the sacred station is mentioned next?
questions.answer: The lesson that only Allah is truly God.

questions.question: Who are named with Allah in bearing witness to this truth?
questions.answer: The angels and those who have knowledge.

questions.question: What moral quality is clearly connected to Allah in that verse?
questions.answer: Justice.

questions.question: In the summary sentence, what title shows that Allah depends on nothing?
questions.answer: Necessary Existent.

questions.question: What title shows that Allah has no partner and no equal?
questions.answer: The One, the Unique.

questions.question: What three things are said to belong to Allah?
questions.answer: The beautiful names, the supreme attributes, and the highest similitude.

questions.question: According to the passage, what agrees together in pointing to Allah?
questions.answer: His essence, attributes, names, qualities, and deeds all agree together.

questions.question: What kind of actions show Allah’s control by bringing things into existence?
questions.answer: Creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: How did the truths in the first chapter point to necessary existence?
questions.answer: They did so clearly and directly through their presence and broad reach.

questions.question: How did those truths also point to unity?
questions.answer: Their all-encompassing nature showed that Allah is One.

questions.question: What will change in the second chapter?
questions.answer: The same truths will be presented mainly as proofs of unity.

questions.question: What remains true even after this change in focus?
questions.answer: The truths still point to necessary existence too.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the connection between Allah’s unity and necessary existence?
questions.answer: They are so connected that each one proves the other.

questions.question: What did the writer hope to do with the second chapter?
questions.answer: He hoped to explain its levels in detail like the first chapter.

questions.question: What stopped him from doing that here?
questions.answer: Different obstacles made him keep it short.

questions.question: What part of Allah is being talked about in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s attribute of Speech.

questions.question: What comes from this attribute?
questions.answer: Divine discourse.

questions.question: What does the image of an ocean of ink teach us?
questions.answer: Allah’s words are too many to be finished or fully written.

questions.question: How does the passage describe Divine discourse in size?
questions.answer: It says it is endless.

questions.question: What is one of the easiest ways to know a being is there, according to the passage?
questions.answer: By that being’s speech.

questions.question: What does that idea prove when it is connected to Allah?
questions.answer: It proves Allah’s existence.

questions.question: What other truth does Divine speech testify to along with existence?
questions.answer: Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What are the first two major proofs of this truth named in the passage?
questions.answer: Revelation and inspiration.

questions.question: What is another proof that comes from written guidance?
questions.answer: The sacred books sent from heaven.

questions.question: Which book is described as especially brilliant and complete?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why are readers sent to other parts of the work?
questions.answer: So they can find the longer explanation and proof there.

questions.question: What does the passage say is enough for now?
questions.answer: The light and hidden wisdom in the verse.

questions.question: What core belief is repeated in the verse from Surah Al-Imran?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: Which two groups join in this witness besides Allah?
questions.answer: The angels and people who possess knowledge.

questions.question: What does the verse teach about Allah’s way of ruling?
questions.answer: He rules with justice.

questions.question: What two qualities of Allah close that verse?
questions.answer: Might and wisdom.

questions.question: How is Allah described in the statement summarizing the traveler’s lesson?
questions.answer: As the Necessary Existent, the One, and the Unique.

questions.question: What special honors are said to belong to Allah?
questions.answer: The beautiful names, the highest attributes, and the loftiest similitude.

questions.question: What shows Allah’s necessary existence in His unity according to the passage?
questions.answer: His necessarily existent essence shows it.

questions.question: What agrees with this witness from His essence?
questions.answer: All His sacred attributes, beautiful names, and active deeds agree with it.

questions.question: Which actions in the passage show Allah’s creative power?
questions.answer: Bringing into being, creating, making, and originating.

questions.question: Which actions show Allah’s wise management?
questions.answer: Measuring, shaping, regulating, and directing.

questions.question: Which actions show Allah’s merciful care?
questions.answer: Preserving, administering, and nurturing creation.

questions.question: Which qualities are matched with those three groups of actions?
questions.answer: Will and power, then choice and wisdom, then purpose and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the condition of Allah’s works?
questions.answer: They are carried out with complete order and balance.

questions.question: In the first chapter, what were the nineteen truths mainly counted as?
questions.answer: Proofs of necessary existence.

questions.question: Why were they counted that way first?
questions.answer: Because they showed existence most plainly and clearly.

questions.question: What will they mainly be counted as in the second chapter?
questions.answer: Proofs of Divine unity.

questions.question: Will they stop pointing to necessary existence in the second chapter?
questions.answer: No, they will still point to it indirectly.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the link between unity and necessity?
questions.answer: It says each one is a proof for the other.

questions.question: What had the writer intended to do for this chapter?
questions.answer: He intended to explain its degrees just as he had done before.

questions.question: Why did he leave the explanation short and summary-like?
questions.answer: Because various obstacles forced him to be concise.
